name: Defereggental
kurzbeschreibung: The pristine Defereggental valley in East Tyrol enchants visitors with historic Jagdhausalm, healing thermal waters, and untamed alpine nature.
preis: Valley and hiking trails freely accessible; Staller Sattel pass road toll-free (traffic light control)
oeffnungszeiten: Accessible year-round; high alpine huts open from late May to mid-October
beschreibung:
Overview

The idyllic and historic Defereggental valley lies nestled between the towering peaks of the Rieserferner Group, the Villgraten Mountains, and the glaciated Venediger Range in the heart of East Tyrol. As one of the least developed high-alpine valleys in the entire Eastern Alps, it has preserved its authentic mountain character, deep-rooted farming traditions, and remarkable biodiversity. Carved by the crystalline Schwarzach river, this 60-kilometer-long valley stretches from Huben near Matrei up to the 2,052-meter Staller Sattel border pass connecting Austria to South Tyrol. Picturesque alpine hamlets like Hopfgarten, St. Veit, and St. Jakob charm travellers with time-honoured shingle-roof farmsteads, rich craftsmanship, and sun-kissed slopes. The valley is internationally renowned for the highly mineralized Defereggen Healing Water, sourced from a depth of over 1,850 meters and valued for centuries for soothing dermatological and respiratory ailments.

Route & Requirements

Exploring the Defereggental offers a wide array of outdoor activities for leisure seekers, families, and seasoned alpinists alike. A standout cultural highlight is the hike to the historic Jagdhausalm at the head of the valley, affectionately called the 'Little Tibet of the Alps'. This heritage-protected settlement of fifteen stone dwellings and a stone-built chapel represents Austria's oldest mountain hamlet, dating back to the early 13th century. The route follows a gentle gravel road from the Alpe Stalle parking area through the wild Arvental valley (walking time approx. 2.5 hours, graded easy to moderate, family-friendly). Ambitious mountaineers can ascend the 3,436-meter Hochgall peak or embark on scenic panoramic treks along the Obersee flower trail. Sturdy hiking boots with non-slip profile soles and weatherproof layers are essential for high-altitude walks in the national park.

Visit & Arrival

The valley is accessible year-round via the well-maintained L25 Defereggental road, branching off the B108 Felbertauern highway at Huben and running toll-free through Hopfgarten to St. Jakob. The continuation across the Staller Sattel into South Tyrol is open during snow-free months from late May to late October with automated traffic lights. Public transport is straightforward: take the train to Lienz station and transfer to regional bus line 954, which serves all villages in the valley regularly.

Tips

Combine your excursion with a relaxing tour of the Deferegger Healing Water House in St. Jakob, then savour fresh mountain milk and traditional East Tyrolean Schlipfkrapfen dumplings at the historic Jagdhausalm while taking in glacier-crowned summits.
